title: `.env` is an ephemeral regenerable reflection of the manifest, never the source of truth
context: `.env` files have quietly become the de facto secrets store on many projects. Developers edit them by hand, tools like docker-compose and Node's dotenv library expect them at fixed paths, CI runners copy them around, and the file gets committed by accident on a regular schedule. Removing the `.env` entirely breaks a large amount of tooling that assumes its presence; keeping it as the source of truth reintroduces every failure mode this blueprint exists to end. The middle path is to keep the `.env` shape at the surface where tooling expects it and change its role from authoritative to reflective.
decision: The `.env` file, when present at the repo root, is generated on demand from the Secrets Manager by the env reflector (TAC-903). Every run of `secrets reflect --deployable <id> --env <env>` overwrites the file atomically with the current vendor-resolved values for the target slice; nothing outside the reflector may write the file, and no runtime code reads the file to bypass the Secrets Manager client. The `.env` path is gitignored at project root by requirement (AC-8106-2) and the reflector refuses to run when it is not (defence against a mis-configured `.gitignore`). Per-environment reflection variants (`.env.dev`, `.env.ci`, `.env.live`) are selected by the `--env` flag; each variant is written and overwritten independently.
consequences: Local tooling that expects `.env` keeps working; the developer runs the reflector and the file appears with values that match the current vendor state. The reflection is discardable at any moment (delete the file, rerun the reflector, get an identical result), which makes the file's ephemerality visible in the workflow. A stale `.env` from a week ago is a shape drift no one has to argue about; the reflector regenerates it. A CI job that needs a `.env` runs the reflector as a preamble; the file exists for the job's runtime and disappears with the runner. A process that reads `.env` directly at boot instead of the client is caught by the source-tree scan (AC-8106-3).

alternativesConsidered.name: No `.env` at all; every consumer reads the client directly
alternativesConsidered.summary: Refuse to write a reflection; every tool that needs a value invokes the CLI or imports the client.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Purer but breaks a lot of tooling with hard-coded `.env` expectations (docker-compose, some Node frameworks' hot-reload modes, some IDE integrations). The reflector adds surface but keeps the ecosystem workable.

alternativesConsidered.name: Commit an encrypted `.env` and decrypt in place
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ship the reflection encrypted at rest in the repo and decrypt to a plaintext `.env` at boot.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Overlaps the default vendor's own encrypt-and-commit posture (ADR-902's SOPS files) without adding anything; the plaintext `.env` still exists on disk during runtime and is now redundant with the encrypted store.
